paper_metadata.title: Tailoring the specific strength of AlNbTiZr high entropy alloys via Si doping

evidence.quote: This study systematically investigates the effects of Si alloying on the microstructure evolution and mechanical properties of Al13Nb29Ti29Zr29 LRHEAs.

For Si0 alloy, the average length of the primary dendrites is approximately 500 μm, and that of the secondary dendrites is about 150 μm

The grain refinement triggered by Si doping can be ascribed to the formation of Zr5Si3 phase, which on one hand increases the core of heterogeneous nucleation, and on the other hand, the eutectic structure fills the dendrite gap to hinder the further growth of dendrites

This results in a simultaneous increase in the specific strength and plasticity

the B2 coherent precipitated phases with a size of 3–7 nm are stably distributed in the BCC matrix and maintains good compatibility with the matrix due to its low mismatch interface. Such fine coherent precipitates can effectively pin dislocations and significantly increase the critical shear stress
